Subject: Annual API commit — looking for options

Hi Laura / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — FastFin's engineering and product teams are excited about Redwood's latency and cost numbers. We're trying to put together an annual purchasing plan for hosted API usage and want something predictable for forecasting and SRE quotas. A few quick asks:  

- Can you share a simple tiered commit framework (Starter / Growth / Enterprise) with per-token pricing for each tier and what discounts look like versus on-demand?
- Do you support quarterly true-ups or staged ramp commitments (we will likely start small and scale through the year)?
- Any standard onboarding credits, first-year discounts, or committed-rate guarantees you apply?

We're the external procurement contact — cc'ing our head of platform (Miguel) on follow-ups if useful. Looking to get internal approval in two weeks, so a short proposal would be ideal.

Thanks,
Caroline

Caroline — great to hear FastFin found the demo useful. High level reply below; attaching a compact spreadsheet and a recommended SOW template for procurement.

Summary (short):
- We recommend a three-tier annual commit ladder with optional quarterly true-ups and a built-in month-to-month overage rate.
- Starter: 100M tokens/year — list price $0.0008/token; committed rate $0.0006/token (25% discount vs on-demand).
- Growth: 500M tokens/year — list $0.0008/token; committed rate $0.00045/token (44% discount).
- Enterprise: 2B+ tokens/year — list $0.0008/token; committed rate $0.00030/token (62.5% discount).

Flexible terms we offer:
- Quarterly true-up window (one-time quarterly adjustment) to move between tiers without penalty if consumption consistently exceeds bucket.
- Ramp schedule: customers can predefine a staged ramp (e.g., 20/30/50% across Q1-Q3) — unused committed tokens roll forward within the year for predictable teams.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $10k credit applied against first invoice on new annual commits > $75k ARR equivalent.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you like the above, we'll send a concise proposal with the exact token math, DocuSign LOI, and an optional 60-day pilot addendum.
2) Karthik — can you review suggested per-token brackets and advise if we should propose a graded mid-tier rate at 1B tokens?
3) Caroline — if Miguel or procurement prefers a different cadence (monthly vs quarterly true-up) tell us your preference and we'll adapt.

Attaching: redwood_commit_tiers_v1.xlsx, SOW-template.pdf

Best,
Laura Bennett

Laura / Karthik — forwarding my notes after a quick sync with the solutions team. High level negotiation posture below (keeps us competitive but preserves margin):

1) Offer the three tiers as Laura suggested but add a mid-step at 1B tokens/year with a committed rate of $0.000375/token to give customers a better jump from Growth -> Enterprise.
2) Keep quarterly true-ups but limit mid-year downward reclassification (they can move up freely; moving down limited to once/year to avoid churn gaming).
3) Add a one-time ramp credit: if they sign > $150k ARR equivalent, provide $25k onboarding credit + 2-week free priority support during initial rollout.
4) For procurement: propose a 60-day pilot LOI (non-binding) with explicit cancellation windows and automatic conversion into the annual commit if usage meets the agreed thresholds.

Related: HubSpot deal id FF-2026-042 shows estimated ARR at $180k in year 1 with projected burst months in Nov/Dec. Keep that in mind for price concessions.
